clue.text: Street Arab makes a thousand in profit

indicators.note: the thousand sits in the profit, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: to profit is to gain
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: An urchin on the streets earns a tidy thousand from some deal.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside GAIN. 'Street Arab' is an old term for a homeless street child.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamin is a street urchin, which is what the dated phrase 'street Arab' described.

clue.text: A boy leaving home makes mischief

parts.note: a person leaving home is going
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad moving out gets up to no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on are dubious happenings or misbehaviour.

clue.text: He has an appointment with official authority

parts.note: a man is a he
a date is an appointment

explanation.surface: A man has a meeting with an official.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an authorisation or commission granted officially.

clue.text: Mention only the north, south and west

parts.words: only the north, south and west
parts.note: three compass points are listed and the fourth is pointedly left out, so the picture is a phrase about that missing point

explanation.surface: A speaker talks of every region but the east.
explanation.walkthrough: N, S and W with no E reads as NOT E.
explanation.definitionFit: To note is to remark on or point out.

clue.text: Hear! Hear! A cathedral city needs assistance

parts.note: Wells is a small cathedral city in Somerset, England
aid means assistance

explanation.surface: Applause greets news that a cathedral city needs help.
explanation.walkthrough: WELLS, in Somerset, is England's smallest cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Hear! Hear!' is the cry of approval used when someone speaks aptly, the same praise as the exclamation.

clue.text: Egalitarian aim of the Worker's Educational Association?

definitions.text: Egalitarian aim of the Worker's Educational Association?

parts.words: Egalitarian aim of the Worker's Educational Association?
parts.note: the aim of making the social classes level, read playfully as the adult-education body's night lessons

explanation.surface: Speculating about the political goal of an adult education charity.
explanation.walkthrough: The Workers' Educational Association is a British adult-education charity; it runs lessons after work, which read as levelling the classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult-education lessons held after the working day, the staple of such associations.

clue.text: See a church beside a stretch of Scottish water

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A view of a church beside a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A loch is a Scottish lake or sea inlet.

clue.text: Football team featured in a magazine

definitions.meaning: a store for arms and ammunition

explanation.surface: A football club gets a write-up in a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a London football club, and an arsenal is a store of weapons, an arms magazine.

clue.text: He acquires twin daughters in twenty-four hours

indicators.note: the daughters are found in the day, one piece inside the other

parts.note: a day lasts twenty-four hours
D is short for daughter, so two of them give DD

explanation.surface: A man becomes father of twin girls in a single day.
explanation.definitionFit: Daddy is a childish word for one's father, a male parent.

clue.text: The government somehow isn't held in high esteem

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are held inside the word for esteem

parts.note: admiration is high esteem

indicators.note: somehow tells us the letters of isn't are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of isn't, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A complaint that the ruling party is not well regarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' scrambles the letters of isn't, and 'held in' tucks the result inside the word for high esteem; the surface reads as a complaint about an unpopular government.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the administration is the executive, the governing body in office.

clue.text: Fired with the dieting craze

indicators.note: a craze sends the letters of the word dieting into a frenzy, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone got all fired up by the latest diet fad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craze' looks like a noun for a fad, but it signals rearranging DIETING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fired has been set alight, kindled into flame.

clue.text: Covered a trial in the final stages

indicators.note: the trial is set in the final stages, one piece inside the other

parts.note: the end is the final stage of something
a case is a trial in court

explanation.surface: A court trial was reported on as it reached its conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covered' looks like the reporting of a trial, but it is the definition; 'final stages' is just the end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Encased means wrapped or enclosed in a casing, that is covered all round.

clue.text: Clothes which people drive in

definitions.meaning: informal word for one's outfit or kit
a motorist drives in first, second or top

explanation.surface: Garments people wear behind the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is informal for clothing, and a car is driven in one of its gears, such as top or reverse.

clue.text: Less than ten really appreciate the thing

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it a lot
it stands for the thing being spoken of

explanation.surface: A fan says there are fewer than ten things they truly love.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of the numerals 0 to 9 is under ten, which is what the definition is pointing at.
explanation.definitionFit: A single numeral runs from zero to nine, so any such figure is under ten.

clue.text: One the other hand, it's just

definitions.meaning: used as a conjunction meaning but or except that

explanation.surface: Weighing a point, someone concedes it is merely fair.
explanation.definitionFit: As a conjunction 'only' means but or however, and as an adverb it means merely.

clue.text: Colour that is fashionable in binding

indicators.note: the fashionable letter goes in the binding, one inside the other

parts.note: tape is used for binding
U means upper-class or socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A trendy shade for the cover of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: U, for upper-class, is a crossword stand-in for posh or fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Taupe is a brownish-grey shade, like moleskin.

clue.text: Temporary lodgings for politicians going to California

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Short-stay housing for lawmakers on a trip to the West Coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Camps are sites of tents or huts used as short-term shelter.

clue.text: Working with the board in the theatre

definitions.text: Working with the board in the theatre

parts.words: Working with the board in the theatre
parts.note: reads like an actor treading the boards, but the theatre is a hospital's operating room, and the board is the surface the surgeon works on

explanation.surface: An actor at work on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage; it is the operating theatre, where the piece of furniture is a working board.
explanation.definitionFit: The surgical table in an operating room is the board on which a patient lies during surgery.

clue.text: She is a beautiful Italian

parts.note: taken as written
bella is the Italian for beautiful

explanation.surface: Praise for a lovely woman from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is a woman's name, so a female person.

clue.text: Are they worn to prevent the floor-covering getting worn?

definitions.text: Are they worn to prevent the floor-covering getting worn?

parts.words: Are they worn to prevent the floor-covering getting worn?
parts.note: a whimsical theory that soft indoor shoes are named because they protect the rug from wear

explanation.surface: A mock-serious question about the purpose of soft indoor footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft indoor footwear, once often made of rug-like fabric, worn around the house.

clue.text: Being devoted to a party faction

parts.note: a do is a party
a ring is a clique or faction

explanation.surface: Loyal to a political group.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring means loving deeply or worshipping.

clue.text: The listener's complaint

parts.note: a complaint here is an ailment, and the organ for listening is what suffers it

explanation.surface: A radio audience member's grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the ear is an ailment of the organ we hear with.

clue.text: Ladies and gentlemen in Franglais

parts.note: the signs on public toilet doors, 'Ladies' and 'Gentlemen', name the facilities; the slang plural sounds like a French plural tacked on an English word

explanation.surface: Addressing an audience in a mix of French and English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' and 'Gentlemen' are what British public toilets are labelled; the word for those rooms is informal British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Public conveniences are labelled for ladies and gents, and the British slang plural for toilets has a French air.

clue.text: Many overcharge with little hesitation when he's standing in

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
o/c is an abbreviation for overcharge
um is a brief hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Hesitant complaints about high fees from a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric who fills in for another temporarily.

clue.text: Idle talk about America by a mathematician

indicators.note: the idle talk goes about, or around, the abbreviation for America

parts.note: gas is idle chatter
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: Gossip about America from a number-cruncher.
explanation.walkthrough: Carl Friedrich GAUSS was a great German mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Friedrich Gauss was a renowned German mathematician of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Caterpillar food

definitions.meaning: informal word for something to eat

explanation.surface: A larva that is also something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is an insect larva like a caterpillar, and in slang it also means something to eat.

clue.text: Heads or tails, it's all the same

indicators.note: the letters read the same in either direction, front to back or back to front

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A coin toss where the result does not matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The ANNA was an old Indian coin, and a coin is what has heads or tails.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a former coin of India, and coins come up heads or tails.

clue.text: What person gets a command low down?

indicators.note: in a down entry the letter is placed lower, beneath the first part

parts.note: who asks what person

explanation.surface: Someone receives an order from below.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, A placed 'low down' comes after WHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the call to a horse to stop.

clue.text: A man of honour, and one opposed to wine

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
I is the Roman numeral for one
anti means opposed

explanation.surface: An honourable gentleman and a teetotaller who objects to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is a Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red Italian vintage from Tuscany.

clue.text: I teach new apprentice in accordance with professional rules

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of I teach are made into something fresh

parts.note: L is the learner sign, for a novice or apprentice

explanation.surface: A teacher instructs a trainee in the code of conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns I TEACH into ETHICA; L is from the learner plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical conduct follows the moral code set for a profession.

clue.text: I'm taken aback by cereal food additive causing a headache

indicators.note: taken aback suggests surprise, but here it means read back to front

parts.note: the letters of I'm, without the apostrophe
grain is cereal
an E or E-number is a food additive code

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked that an additive in their cereal gives them a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns IM into MI. E-numbers are codes for EU-approved additives.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe recurring head pain.

clue.text: For many gladiators it proved a near disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves the letters of a near in ruins, rearranged

explanation.surface: Many gladiators came close to catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' signals rearranging A NEAR; the definition is the place gladiators fought.
explanation.definitionFit: The amphitheatre floor was where gladiators fought, often to the death.
